data.name: Ross
data.gender_notes: Ross is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Anglo-Saxon name derived from the Old English word ros, meaning 'head' or 'red'. The name was originally given to children with red hair, and later came to mean 'chief' or 'redhead'. The name Ross carries the meaning “Red head” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Ross usually hope their child will grow to embody red head and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Ross represents the strength and vitality of the redhead, as well as the leadership qualities associated with being a 'chief'. It is also a reminder of the connection between nature and spirituality, as the name comes from the Old English word for 'head' and the Celtic word for 'red'.
